To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

behavioral interventions and pharmacotherapy can be effective for weight loss in patients with obesity, and that genomics research may provide valuable insights for the development of new pharmacologic treatments.

1) lifestyle modification is effective in inducing clinically significant weight loss; 2) lifestyle modification reduces the risk of diabetes mellitus in patients with impaired glucose tolerance; 3) lifestyle modification may reduce cardiovascular morbidity in patients with diabetes; 4) lifestyle modification is more effective when combined with pharmacotherapy; 5) pharmacotherapy, alone, is less effective in inducing weight loss than lifestyle modification; and 6) genomics research may yield novel targets for weight loss drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new treatments for obesity and its complications.
the development of novel behavioral and pharmacologic treatments for obesity.
the prevention and treatment of obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective treatment of obesity is the one that is most likely to be followed by the patient, and this is most likely to occur if the treatment is enjoyable and easy.
the best way for an individual to lose weight is to eat less and move more, and that pharmacologic therapy should be reserved for those patients who are unable or unwilling to do this.
the treatment for obesity is not yet fully understood, and there is a need for further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of behavioral and pharmacologic therapies is likely to provide the greatest benefit for the management of obesity and related comorbidities.
obesity is an important public health problem and a major cause of morbidity and mortality.
the combination of diet, behavior modification and physical exercise is the best treatment for obesity, but that pharmacotherapy may be helpful in certain individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is a complex disorder that requires a comprehensive approach to treatment.
the best way to lose weight is to eat less food, exercise more and to do it consistently over the long term.
we are making progress in the fight against obesity, and we are doing so in a manner that will benefit patients and their physicians.
